name: CO-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Pettersen's overwhelming fundraising edge: $2.2M raised and $1.2M on hand versus roughly $102K for Bennett
District's D+8 partisan lean combined with incumbency
Prediction markets price the race near 97% Democratic
No public general-election polling, keeping uncertainty wide
model.rationale: A Democratic incumbent in a district leaning eight points Democratic faces a challenger who has raised little and has almost nothing banked, while markets and fundamentals alike point to a comfortable win. The evidence points the same direction on every measure, so there is no basis to move off a roughly twenty-point margin.
model.watch: A sharp national shift toward Republicans or a late wave of outside spending against Pettersen could narrow the margin, though the resource gap leaves little time to close it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brittany Pettersen, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Denver-area district that leans Democratic by about eight points. No public general-election polling is available, so the picture rests on fundamentals. She has raised roughly $2.2 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Tim Bennett has raised about $102,000 with under $12,000 remaining. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but show little financial activity.

Prediction markets put her chances near 97 percent, and the district's eight-point Democratic lean points the same way. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polls, which keeps the error range wide despite lopsided resources and partisanship. A national environment sharply worse for Democrats, paired with a last-minute surge in outside spending for the challenger, would be needed to put the seat in doubt.
